transcript.content: Hello, welcome in. What brings you to see me today?

I, uh... I came in because I just keep feeling like I’ve completely let my family down by taking on this mortgage. It’s... it's just a lot. The house actually has this huge oak tree in the front yard, which is nice, but the roots are totally messing up the concrete on the driveway. I spent like three hours watching YouTube videos on how to fix driveway cracks last weekend, but then the algorithm just started showing me videos of guys building log cabins from scratch out in the woods, and I ended up watching those until like 3 AM. I always thought it'd be cool to just live off the grid like that, you know? Not have to worry about property taxes or HOA fees... 

But, um, what was I saying? Right, the mortgage. It just weighs on me so much. Like, every small mistake I make at work—I wait tables, so if I drop a fork or punch in the wrong appetizer—it just proves I’m completely useless. I just get this heavy feeling that I deserve whatever bad things happen to me.
{"intent": "Screen for history of hypomanic or manic episodes to differentiate bipolar disorder from unipolar depression", "question": "Have you ever had periods lasting a few days or more where

Where I... what, like had a ton of energy or didn't need sleep? No, not really. I'm pretty much always just drained. 

I mean, I try drinking coffee to get through my shifts, but it doesn't even do anything anymore. We actually have this massive industrial espresso machine at the restaurant, one of those really fancy Italian ones with all the shiny chrome. It completely broke down on Tuesday right in the middle of the lunch rush. This one regular—he always comes in and orders a double macchiato, always tips exactly eight percent, which is just insulting—he threw an absolute fit about it. I tried to explain that the boiler was shot, but he just kept tapping his watch at me. People can be so incredibly impatient, you know? It really makes you wonder why they even bother going out to sit down at a restaurant if they're in such a massive hurry to leave. I'd rather just eat at home, honestly. 

But, um... sorry, what were we talking about? Oh, right, those periods of time. Yeah, no, I don't really get energized or anything like that. Just mostly that heavy feeling.

{"intent": "Assess how long the low, drained mood has been present to differentiate between an acute depressive episode and persistent depressive disorder", "question": "How long have you been experiencing

How long have I been feeling like this? Um... I guess this whole heavy, guilty thing has been going on for about a year and two months now. 

It actually started right around the time my car failed inspection. It was the catalytic converter, which is just ridiculously expensive to replace. The mechanic I took it to—this guy named Frank, he has this massive German Shepherd that just wanders around the garage while he works—he told me it would be cheaper to just buy a new car. The dog was actually really sweet, though. I threw a tennis ball for him for like twenty minutes while I was waiting for the estimate. I've always wanted a dog, but my landlord is super strict about the pet policy. He even tried to evict the woman in 3B because she had a goldfish, which just seems a little extreme, right? Like, what kind of damage is a goldfish going to do to an apartment? 

But, uh, anyway... yeah. A year and a couple months of just feeling like a complete failure.

{"intent": "Assess whether symptoms of inattention and distractibility have been present since childhood to evaluate for ADHD", "question": "Growing up as a child, did you struggle with being easily distracted,

Did I struggle with being distracted as a kid? Um, no, not really. I mean, I did pretty well in school, mostly. I was actually in this advanced reading program in fourth grade. We got to sit on these giant beanbag chairs in the back of the library instead of regular desks. They were that bright, neon green color that was so popular back in the nineties, you know? Actually, my cousin had a windbreaker that exact same color. He wore it everywhere, even in the summer when it was like ninety degrees out. He ended up moving to Florida to work at a reptile sanctuary, which is wild because he used to be terrified of snakes when we were little. We found a garter snake in the backyard once and he literally screamed and climbed up on top of the picnic table. 

But, um, what was the question? Oh, being distracted. No, I don't think so. I was pretty focused back then.
Have you lost interest or pleasure in doing things you normally enjoy?

Lost interest? Um, yeah, I'd say so. Like, I used to always joke around with the regulars at the restaurant, and I'd usually text my brother right after my shifts to catch up. 

My brother actually just got one of those new folding smartphones. It's so weird, it looks like a little square coaster from the outside but then it opens up into this giant screen. I don't really get why you'd want a screen with a visible crease right down the middle of it, honestly. Plus, he dropped it like two days after he bought it, which is just classic him. He's always been super clumsy. When we were kids, he knocked over our mom's favorite lamp—it was this really ugly ceramic owl, but she loved it for some reason—and he tried to glue it back together with just regular white school glue. It looked absolutely terrible, you could see the glue dripping down the owl's beak. 

But, uh... sorry, what were you asking? Oh, right, enjoying things. Yeah, I just don't really do any of that anymore. I mostly just keep my face straight at work now, say only what I have to, and get it over with. And when my brother texts me, I just let the messages sit there. I just don't really feel the pull to answer anybody.
During this time, have you had any thoughts of death or thoughts of wanting to hurt yourself?

Thoughts of death? Um... I mean, I don't have a plan to hurt myself or anything like that. But sometimes, when I'm lying awake before an early shift... 

I hate those early shifts, honestly. You have to be there at like 5:30 in the morning to set up the coffee stations and roll the silverware. And the silverware is always still hot from the dishwasher, which sounds nice, but it actually kind of burns your fingers if you're not careful. One time, the dishwasher—this guy named Leo, who is super into amateur wrestling—he accidentally loaded a plastic ramekin into the high-heat cycle and it completely melted over the heating element. The whole kitchen smelled like burning tires for three days. We had to keep all the back doors propped open, which let all these flies in, and the manager was furious. He made Leo buy these special fly traps that look like little paper lanterns, but they didn't even work. 

But, um, anyway... yeah. When I'm lying awake before those shifts, I just... I sometimes think it would be easier if I just didn't wake up. Like, if I just didn't have to get out of bed and keep failing at everything, you know? It just feels like it would be a relief.
